title: Pneumonic Plague in Focus After Researcher's Death in Russia
seoTitle: Pneumonic Plague in Focus After Researcher's Death in.
subtitle: The Case That Led to Quarantine and Surveillance in Irkutsk
excerpt: The death of a 28-year-old researcher at a Russian plague institute raised suspicions of pneumonic plague, leading to quarantines and medical surveillance in Irkutsk.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: O GLOBO, CNN Brasil, Jovem Pan
contentHtml:
The death of Darya Shipilova, a 28-year-old employee of the Siberian Anti-Plague Research Institute, in a Shelekhov hospital, triggered quarantine and surveillance in Irkutsk. The cause of the pneumonia that killed her remains unknown, but rumors of a laboratory accident involving bacteria fueled public concern.

Why the Topic Is Trending Now

News of Shipilova's death and the quarantine measures in hospitals in the region generated immediate repercussions, as it involves the possibility of pneumonic plague, a serious disease potentially transmissible between people.

What Rospotrebnadzor Says

The Russian health surveillance agency stated that exhaustive analyses did not detect microorganisms related to Shipilova's activities. The pneumonia was classified as of unknown etiology, and no evidence of safety protocol violations was found.

Quarantine and Surveillance Measures

Shelekhov Hospital was placed under quarantine, halting patient admissions and discharges, while the laboratory suspended routine analyses. In Irkutsk, hospitals and a maternity ward adopted quarantine measures, and individuals who had contact with Shipilova were placed under medical supervision.

What the WHO and CDC Said

The World Health Organization is in contact with Russian authorities to verify the tests performed and assess potential international implications. The U.S. CDC is monitoring the situation and remains prepared to respond to a potential case of pneumonic plague in the country.

What Remains Unclear

There is no proof that Shipilova contracted pneumonic plague or that her death was caused by pathogens she handled. The investigation continues to determine the exact cause of the pneumonia and whether there was a laboratory accident.
